items.title: Kent Jordan interviewed by Monk Rowe, Rome, New York, August 22, 2006
items.q: performing with people like Alvin Batiste

ctx.x: Oh well let me mention this in the archive for you. Lu and Charlie’s was a very interesting venue. It was a club. It was owned by, oh my good friend, now Charlie Bering, who passed away maybe about six years ago. And Charlie was actually one of the producers of the Jazz and Heritage Festival but he had a club when I was in high school. And people like Alvin Batiste performed there, Ellis Marsalis performed there, all of the local New Orleans jazz giants performed there. And that was my first baptism into jazz and…

and people like James Black on drums and all these wonderful musicians. I mean I was like in heaven, I was like a child in a candy shop. You know, like studying with Ellis during the daytime and performing with people like Alvin Batiste, I was still at that time performing with my father and you know they were bringing other musicians who love New Orleans, like Cannonball Adderley —
